Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 4:00 pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be
summarized by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City
Council and will also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be
recorded for public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City

  3
 Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers first. After all speakers in the Chambers have spoken,
the Presiding Officer will call upon those participating via zoom or teleconference.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, virtually, email, phone call, mail and any other method which may become
available. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such times when a State of
Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email
at yglaze@sogate.org.

STJBJECT: PROrOSED  AMENDMENTS  TO THE  SOUTH GAT4 ZONING  CODE (TITL.E 11)
CONCERNING  DEVELOPMENT  STANDARDS,  LAND  USE  CLASSIFICATION  AND
DF,VF,LOPMENT  REVIEW  PROCEDURES.

PURPOSE: To update City Council on a work program to update Municipal Code Title 11 (Zoning), prior
to staff returning with a formally drafted ordinance for Planning Commission recotmnendation and City
Council consideration.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  Receive and File.

BACKGROUND:  Planning Division  staff identified  a work program to update City of South Gate
Municipal Code Title 11, Zoning, to allow greater flexibility  in development standards, improve aesthetics
in commercial corridors and city gateways, streatnline the development review process, and establish high
performance standards for the built environment,  Staff compiled a set of proposed Code Amendments
addressing land use classifications, developmentand  design standards, and developmentreview  procedures.

Staff presented the proposed Code Amendments  to the Planning  Commission  at study sessions on March
17, 2026 and April 7, 2026. The Planning Commission reviewed staff's initial recommendations,  asked
clarifying  questiorrs, and provided preliminary  direction on several items, while requesting additional
information  and data on other items,  The proposed Code Amendments  w'll retut'n to the Planning
Commission  at a future date, as a formally  drafted ordinance,  for the Planning  Commission's
recommendationto  the City Council for final consideration and adoption.

DISCUSSION/ANALYSIS:

The following  proposed Zoning Code Amendments  were presented to the Planriing  Commission  and the
Commission's  feedback is outlined below:

Table 11.21-4  Commercial  Industrial  Zones Allowed  Land  Uses (Chapter  11.21 Land  Use Types)

  Prohibit  Concrete  or Cement  Manufacturing.  Concrete manufacturxng  uses are only permitted  with
  conditional  use permit  (C{JP)  approval  in  the  M2  (Light  Manufacg)  and  M3  (Heavy
  Manufacturing)  Zones due to the intensity  of the t'ise that involves  outdoor storage of cement materials,

  I
  9
  heavy  industrial  equipment,  and regular  truck  trips.  The M2 and M3 zones are concentrated  primarily
 in areas along  the Union  Pacific  railroad  near the intersection  of Firestone  Blvd  and Atlantic  Avenue
 and East of the 710 Freeway  along  Garfield  Avenue.  Staff recommends  amending  the Code to prohibit
 concrete  manufacturing  in the M2  and M3  zones. The code modification  would  prohibit  new cement
 manufacturing  businesses  and limit  expansion  of existing  cement  manufacturing  businesses.

Planning  Commission  feedback:  The Cornrnission  expressed  consistent  support  at both sessions  for a
citywide  prohibition,  citing  dust and environmental  health  concerns  for nearby  residents  and South Gate
Park.

Modify  Vehicle  Services,  Repair/Storage.  Vehicle  services  repair/storage  uses are permitted  by-right
in the M2  and M3 zones  and by CUP  approval  in the IF (Industrial  Flex),  CDRI  (Corridor  1), CDR2
(Corridor  2) zones.  The proposed  amendment  prohibits  vehicle  storage  as a primary  use only and would
allow  vehicle  storage  as an accessory  use to vehicle  repair  uses.  Outdoor  vehicle  storage  would  be
restricted  to rear or side areas of vehicle  services  buildings  where  vehicle  services  are conducted.

Planning  Commission  feedback:  The Commission  supported limiting  storage to an accessory use tied to active
vehicle  repair, capped at 15 consecutive  days and restricted  to side/rear yards, and directed  staff to extend the
same standard to the Tweedy Boulevard  Specific  Plan area in response to resident complaints  there.

Vehicle  Towing.  Vehicle  towing  services  are only permitted  by-right  in the M2 and M3 zones.  Staff
recommends  requiring  CUP approval  for vehicle  towing  services  in order  to ensure towing  operations
maintain  public  safety, orderly  traffic  flow  on nearby  public  streets and preserve  community  aesthetics.

Planning  Commission  Direction:  The Planning  Commission  supported requiring  a CUP for vehicle towing uses,
which would give the City the ability  to condition  future towing  operations.

Truck  Storage/Terminals.  Truck  storage  uses are only allowed  by CUP approval  in M2 and M3 zones.
Staff recommends  the Planning  Commission  consider  the merits  of prohibiting  truck  storage  uses in all
zones  in the City.  Truck  storage  activities  may  result  in noise  impacts  from  truck  activity,  increased
traffic  congestion,  increased  air pollution,  visual  blight,  and street pavement  impacts.

Planning  Commission  feedback:  The Planning  Commission  did not reach consensus and requested additional
data on traffic,  air quality, and land value impacts before choosing between an outright prohibition  and conditional
allowance with parameters. The Commission  also directed  staff to close the "parking  fleets"  loophole  so that it
excludes truck/semi storage.

Storage  Facilities.  Storage  facilities  are permitted  by CUP approval  in the LI (Light  Industrial)  and by-
right  in the M3  zone.  Staff  recommends  prohibiting  storage  facilities  as a primary  use, but allowing
storage  facilities  as an accessory  use in order to preserve  land for higher-value  and job generating  uses.

Planning  Commission  feedback:  The Planning  Commission  supported  not allowing  mini-storage  as a
by-right  primary  use in the LI/M2  zones,  permitting  it only  as an accessory  use to encourage  mixed
development,  and directed  staff to provide  a map/count  of existing  facilities  and to use the clearer  term
"mini-storage"  to avoid  confusion  with  general  warehousing.

  10
 Table 11.21-3  Allowed  Land  Uses, Urban  Mixed-Use  Zones  (Chapter  11.21  Land  Use Types)

  Laundromats:  Laundromats  are currently  not listed explicitly  as a permitted  use.  Laundromats  were
  previously  listed  as a conditionally  permitted  use in Title  11, Zoning,  prior  to 2015.  Staff has relied  on
  a determination  that laundromats  are most  similar  to "Laundry  Agencies"  (less than 2,500  sq. ft.) and
  "Laundry  Plants"  (2,500  sq. ft. or larger),  although  these terms  in other cities  are not intended  for self-
  servicelaundryfacilities.  Staffrecommendsidentifyinglaundromatsonthelandusetableandallowing
  the use as a conditionally  permitted  use in the Urban  Mixed  Use zones with  a minimum  separation  of
  500 'ft from  other laundromats.

  Planning  Commission  feedback:  The Planning  Commission  supported  creating  a distinct  "laundromat"
  land  use  category,  defined  separately  from  "laundry  agency/plant,"  requiring  a CUP,  and  clearly
  distinguishing  self-service  coin laundromats  from  dry cleaning  and industrial-scale  laundry  plants  (given
  safety  concerns  related  to dry  cleaning  chemical  solvents).  The  Commission  asked  staff  to research
  neighboring-city  standards  and return  with  a refined  distance/size  proposal.  The  Commission  also
  directed  that existing  laundromats  be grandfathered  as legal non-conforming  uses, subject  to compliance
  only  if they expand.

Ground-floor  retail  and pedestrian  uses (11.23.070)

  Storefront  Transparency:  Staff recommends  modifying  retail  storefront  guidelines  into standards  that
  can be enforced  for existing  businesses.  The guideline  currently  limits  obscuring  the view  of windows
  by no more than 25%.  Additional  language  would  prohibit  ground  floor  windows  from  being  opaque

  or tinted.  Product  displays  would  be prohibited  from  obscuring  visibility  into the store.

  Planning  Commission  feedback:  The  Plaru'iing  Commission  supported  prohibiting  opaque/tinted
  ground-floor  windows  and displays  that obscure  visibility,  for safety  and pedestrian  activation,  while
  allowing  room  for temporary  shade allowances  for sun or product  protection.

Security  Fencing  (11.30.070)

  Security  fencing:  Barbed  wire  is identified  as a prohibited  fencing  type  in all zoning  districts,  but is
  prevalent  at many  industrial  businesses  throughout  the City.  Section  11.30.070  provides  the ability  for
  the Director  to consider  additional  fencing  design  features  in LI, M2, and M3 zones for security  fencing
  on a case-by-case  basis.  Staff recommends  the Planning  Commission  discuss  the existing  case-by-case
  security  fencing  exception.  If  the  Planning  Commission  were  to explore  restricting  barbed  wire

  considerations  on a case-by-case  basis,  staff would  recommend  that barbed  wire  fencing  be permitted
  on a case-by-case,  but restricted  to areas not visible  from  public  street view.

  Planning  Commission  feedback:  The Planning  Commission  provided  consistent  direction  across both
  sessions  to restrict  barbed/razor  wire  to areas not visible  from  public  streets  on a case-by-case  basis
  (similar  to the City  of Downey's  approach)  rather  than  an outright  ban, and directed  staff  to conduct
  business  outreach  before  finalizing  the standard.

Prohibited  Signs  (11.36.050)

  Prohibit  Cabinet/Box  Signs:  Staff  recommends  including  cabinet/box  signs  in the list of prohibited
  signs  to improve  the visual  quality  of commercial  corridors,  reduce  bulky  signs,  encourage  higher
  quality  sign designs,  and prevent  excessive  illumination.

  11
   Rooftop  Signs.  Rooftop  signs are currently  prohibited,  which  is a commonly  adopted  prohibition  in the
  sign ordinances  of other  cities.  Staff recommends  maintaining  the prohibition  unless  approved  by the
  Planning  Commission  as part of a sign program  for a major  shopping  center visible  from  the 710 or 105
  Freeway  and  determined  to be of  a superior  architectural  design.  There  are many  examples  of
  destination  commercial  areas in California  that  include  rooftop  signs  that  maintain  a high  aesthetic
  standard  and could  incentivize  economic  development  activity.

  Planning  Commission  Feedback:  The Planning  Commission  supported  prohibiting  new cabinet/box
  sign  installations  citywide,  while  allowing  existing  cabinet  casings  to be re-faced  by new  tenants
  (grandfathered).  The  Commission  supported  maintaining  the rooftop  sign prohibition,  subject  to the
  exception  for a Planning  Commission-approved  major  shopping-center  sign program,  and directed  staff
  to add glare/light-pollution  language  to protect  nearby  residential  areas. The Commission  also supported
  prohibiting  exposed  raceways.

Signs Allowed  by Sign Permit  in Commercial  and Manufacturing  Zone  (11.36.050)

  Establish  a permitted  sign  type:  There  are no requirements  for  sign type  in the sign  ordinance  to
  communicate  the  standard  for  commercial  and  industrial  signs.  Staff  recommends  establishing  a
  standard  for  channel  letters,  push-thru,  or halo-lit  letters  as sign  alternatives.  Painted  signs  would
  continue  to be an allowed  sign type when  approved  by the Director  and demonstrated  to be designed  in
  a superior  quality.

  Establish  a sign type  standard  for freestanding  or ground  signs.  There are no standards  for sign type
  for freestanding  or ground  signs.  Staff recommends  establishing  a standard  of channel,  routed,  halo-lit
  or push-thru  letters.

  Prohibit  Pole Signs.  Staff recommends  prohibiting  pole signs to reduce  visual  clutter  along cornrnercial
  corridors,  improve  community  aesthetic  and streetscape  appearance,  and prevent  oversized  signs that
  dominate  the skyline.

  Planning  Commission  Feedback:  The  Plaru'iing  Cornrnission  supported  requiring  channel,  push-
  through,  cut-through,  or halo-lit  letters,  with  painted  signs  allowed  only  if "superior  quality"  and
  Director-approved,  and asked  staff  to return  with  visual  examples/standards  to define  that term.  The
  Commission's  reaction  to freestanding/monument  sign standards  was mixed,  and staff was directed  to
  bring  back visual  comparisons  before  finalizing.  The Commission  generally  supported  prohibiting  pole
  signs in favor  of monument  signs, contingent  on staff conducting  outreach  to corridor  businesses  beyond
  the Chamber  of Commerce.

Flag  Poles in Nonresidential  Zoning  District  (11.40.250)

  Establish  flagpole  standards  in nonresidential  zoning  districts:  There  are no standards  for flag poles
  citywide.  Staff  recommends  allowing  flag  poles  at a maximum  height  of 25 feet by administrative
  approval  and establishing  a standard  for oversized  flag poles above 25 feet by City  Council  approval  on
  developed  sites of a minimum  10 acres.

  Planning  Commission  Feedback:  General  Support.

  12
 Appeals  (11.50.040)

  Establishacall-upprocedurefordecisionsunderTitlell:  Thereareappealsproceduresfordecisions
  made by approval  authorities  pursuant  to Title 11, but it is unclear  how existing  approval  authorities  can
  appeal  decisions  of lower  decision-making  bodies.  Staff  recommends  adding  a call-up  procedure  to
  allow  the Planning  Commission  the ability  to call-up  administrative  decisions  and City  Council  the
  ability  to call-up  Planning  Commission  decisions.

  Planning  Commission  Feedback:  General  Support.

Conditional  Use Permit  Process "CUP"  (11.52.040)

  Establish  CUP  expiration:  The  Zoning  code  does not  establish  an expiration  for  a CUP.  Staff
  recommends  establishment  of a 2-year  expiration  dates for a CUP and allowthree  1-year  time extensions
  that can be approved  by the Planning  Commission.

  Planning  Commission  Feedback:  General  Support.

Lot Line Adiustment  (12.02.020)

  LotLineAdiustments:  ALotLineAdjustment(LLA)isaprocessthatallowspropertyownerstoadjust
  their  boundary  between  adjacent  parcels  without  creating  a new  lot.  The South  Gate LLA  standards
  require  Planning  Commission  approval,  although  only  tentative  parcel  and tract maps require  Plaru'iing
  Commission  and Council  approval  at a public  hearing.  Surrounding  cities  of Norwalk,  Lynwood,
  Paramount,  Downey,  and Bellflower  allow  LLAs  by approval  of the City  Engineer,  which  reduces  the
  processing  times  for applicants  and city staff.

  Planning  Commission  Feedback:  General  Support  with  substantial  projects  reported  to  the
  Commission.

Maintenance  and Rehabilitation  of Vacant  and Neglected  Buildings  (Add  Chapter  9.47)

  Establish  performance  standards  for vacant/neglected  buildings:  The South  Gate Municipal  Code
  lacks enforcement  tools  for vacant  and neglected  buildings,  resulting  in properties  remaining  fenced  or
  buildings  boarded  up indefinitely.  Staff  recommends  defining  building  and structures  left  vacant  for
  more than 180 days as nuisances  unless:

  1.  Is subject  to an active  building  permit  for repair  or rehab.
  2.  Is actively  being  offered  for sale, lease or rent
  3.  Is actively  maintained  and monitored  including  removal  of perimeter  security  fencing  and window
  boards,  and maintaining  the exterior  free of junk,  trash and debris.

  Planning  Commission  Feedback:  General  Support.

ADDITIONAL  CONSIDERATIONS:

Since the Planning  Commission  study  session,  Councilmembers,  individually  or collectively,  have raised
additional  potential  code  amendments  that  require  Commission  discussion  and  direction.  Staff  also
identified  additional  Code amendments  that require  direction  and prioritization  as follows:

  13
   Distance  restrictions  for certain  land  uses to limit  concentration

  @  Smoke  shops  - Currently  permitted  by right  in the Industrial  Flex  (IF),  Corridor  2 (CDR2),  Urban
  Neighborhood  ({JN),  Regional  Commercial  (RC);  in the Transit  Village  (TV),  Civic
  Center  (CC),  Corridor  1 (CDRI),  Main  Street (MS),  TMU-1  and TMU-2  zones.

  Earber/beauty  shops - Classified  as Personal  Services,  General,  and therefore  permitted  by right  in
  all zones (TV, IF, CC, CDRI,  CDR2,  {JN, MS, RC, LI, TMU-1,  and TMU-2  zones);  prohibited  in
  the M2 and M3 zones.

  Reduce  maximum  building  height  in the  Neighborhood  Low  (NL)  zone  - The  current  standard
  permits  a maximum  of 3 stories  or 45 feet in height  (whichever  is less) on lots under  5,000  square feet.

  Limitations  on side-yard  residential  fencing  adjacent  to vehicle  driveways  - Interior  fencing  on the
  property  line is currently  permitted  up to 36 inches  within  the front-yard  setback,  and up to a maximum
  height  of 6 feet beyond  the front-yard  setback.

*  Special  restrictions  in the M2  and M3 zones - The Municipal  Code envisions  single-use  retail  in the
  M2 and M3 zones, generally  located  between  the Los Angeles  River  and Rio Hondo  River  south of the
